newsitem.title: USA: Waigel - Germany stands by 2.9 pct deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - Germany stands by 2.9 pct deficit forecast.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Sunday that he remained confident that Germany would achieve a budget deficit ratio of 2.9 percent this year and that the government would take further measures if need be to meet that goal.
Speaking to a press briefing ahead of the semi-annual IMF and G7 meetings, Waigel said: "The German government stands by its 2.9 percent deficit forecast for this year."
Waigel was accompanied by Bundesbank President Franz Tietmeyer, who said German monetary policy remains interested in a strong mark.
Tietmeyer, referring to the dollar, said: "The Bundesbank is not interested in foreign exchange market overshoots."
Speaking about the Federal Reserve Board's recent decision to raise interest rates, Waigel said the move was an important signal that the Fed is ready to take pre-emptive strikes against inflation.
The Fed raised the Federal Funds rate on March 25 to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.
